content: 1. Ketoconazole and Cinacalcet: Ketoconazole increases the plasma levels and effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction is significant and may require avoiding the combination or using an alternative drug. 2. Ketoconazole and Clarithromycin: Clarithromycin increases the levels and effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 3. Ketoconazole and Clobazam: Ketoconazole increases clobazam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. This may necessitate dose adjustments and close monitoring due to increased exposure to the active metabolite N-desmethylclobazam. 4. Ketoconazole and Clomipramine: Ketoconazole increases clomipramine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. 5. Ketoconazole and Clonazepam: Ketoconazole increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Ketoconazole and Clopidogrel: Ketoconazole reduces clopidogrel efficacy by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19, which are essential for converting clopidogrel to its active metabolite. This interaction compromises platelet aggregation inhibition, requiring alternative therapy. 7. Ketoconazole and Colchicine: Ketoconazole increases colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp). Co-administration is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Dose adjustments are necessary if co-administration cannot be avoided. 8. Ketoconazole and Conivaptan: Ketoconazole significantly increases conivaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Ketoconazole and Conjugated Estrogens: Ketoconazole increases conjugated estrogen levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-gp. Close monitoring is required, and alternative therapy may be necessary. 10. Ketoconazole and Copanlisib: Ketoconazole increases copanlisib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg and monitor closely. 11. Ketoconazole and Cortisone: Ketoconazole increases cortisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-gp. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Ketoconazole and Crizotinib: Ketoconazole increases crizotinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Ketoconazole and Cyclophosphamide: Ketoconazole increases cyclophosphamide toxicity by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Ketoconazole and Cyclosporine: Ketoconazole increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting P-gp. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 15. Ketoconazole and Dabigatran: Ketoconazole increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting P-gp. Dose adjustments are required based on renal function (CrCl). Avoid co-administration if CrCl <30 mL/min. 16. Ketoconazole and Dapsone: Ketoconazole increases dapsone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ketoconazole and Daridorexant: Ketoconazole increases daridorexant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Ketoconazole and Darifenacin: Ketoconazole increases darifenacin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Darifenacin may also increase ketoconazole levels. Monitor closely, though the clinical significance is unclear. 19. Ketoconazole and Darolutamide: Ketoconazole increases darolutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and P-gp. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed. 20. Ketoconazole and Dasatinib: Ketoconazole increases dasatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Ketoconazole and Dexamethasone: Ketoconazole increases dexamethasone levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Dexamethasone may reduce ketoconazole levels. Monitor closely. 22. Ketoconazole and Diazepam: Ketoconazole increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19. This interaction may increase adverse effects, requiring close monitoring or alternative therapy. 23. Ketoconazole and Diclofenac: Ketoconazole increases diclofenac levels via CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Do not exceed a diclofenac dose of 50 mg twice daily. 24. Ketoconazole and Didanosine: Didanosine reduces ketoconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer ketoconazole 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine. 25. Ketoconazole and Dronabinol: Ketoconazole increases dronabinol levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ketoconazole and Dronedarone: Ketoconazole increases dronedarone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 27. Ketoconazole and Doxorubicin: Ketoconazole increases doxorubicin levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ketoconazole and Doxepin: Both ketoconazole and doxepin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Ketoconazole and Dolasetron: Both ketoconazole and dolasetron prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Ketoconazole and Donepezil: Ketoconazole increases donepezil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Ketoconazole and Doravirine: Ketoconazole increases doravirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations and potential toxicities. 32. Ketoconazole and Disopyramide: Ketoconazole increases disopyramide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, making this combination contraindicated. 33. Ketoconazole and Docetaxel: Ketoconazole increases docetaxel levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ketoconazole and Deflazacort: Ketoconazole increases deflazacort levels via CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibition. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when co-administered.
